scope: Targeted prior-art and metric-comparability review, not an exhaustive novelty search or a new model benchmark

sources.title: Illumination Invariant Image Matching for Lunar TRN
sources.locator: Section III; Section IV; Table 1, p.11
sources.finding: LIMA combines differently lit registered references; the separate lunar-adapted LoFTR achieves RA-1/RA-5 of 84.9/97.3% on 180E and 70.6/85.9% on unseen 0E.
sources.metric: Percentage of predicted matches within 1/5 image pixels; not absolute pose recovery
sources.novelty_boundary: Illumination-aware lunar matching and lunar adaptation already exist.

sources.title: LoMa: Local Feature Matching Revisited
sources.finding: The project page reports LoMa-G 54.3 HardMatch and 73.4 WxBS mAA@10px, plus 84.0 MegaDepth AUC@20deg.
sources.metric: Matching mAA or relative-pose AUC on terrestrial benchmarks
sources.novelty_boundary: These are LoMa-G results, not the pinned LoMa-R profile used in our historical CPU study.

sources.title: RoMa v2: Harder Better Faster Denser Feature Matching
sources.finding: RoMa v2 reports 86.6 MegaDepth-1500 and 73.8 ScanNet-1500 AUC@20deg, using 800px coarse/1024px fine resolution for that comparison.
sources.metric: Relative-pose error AUC, not a binary absolute-pose success rate
sources.novelty_boundary: Subpixel refinement and predicted correspondence covariance already exist.

sources.title: RoMa-Omega: What Feed-Forward 3D Models Know About Image Matching
sources.finding: Within its Table 2, RoMa-Omega/RoMa v2 score 72.9/64.8 on WxBS and 50.0/46.5 on HardMatch (mAA@10px). Runtime Table 5 uses an A100, batch 8.
sources.metric: Matching mAA; GPU throughput under a different hardware/batching protocol
sources.novelty_boundary: A newer general-purpose comparator; its GPU rate cannot establish our CPU speedup.

sources.title: Semi-Dense Matching Uncertainty Is Not Just Local Confidence
sources.finding: A9-parameter error model separates coarse failures from local refinement noise and weights a geometric refit; improvements are not uniform across every metric.
sources.novelty_boundary: Reliability-weighted refitting alone is not a new contribution.

sources.title: Adapting Stereo Vision From Objects To 3D Lunar Surface Reconstruction with the StereoLunar Dataset
sources.finding: Lunar-domain MASt3R adaptation evaluates reconstruction and relative pose. MOONSt3R is the released adapted checkpoint.
sources.metric: Dense reconstruction and relative pose, not our fixed-reference-geometry AP3P protocol
sources.novelty_boundary: Lunar adaptation already exists; investigate shared terrain/data before claiming independent generalization.

sources.title: Geometric Foundation Model Distillation for Efficient Lunar 3D Reconstruction
sources.finding: Distills a 688M lunar MASt3R teacher into students up to 7x smaller; the author page lists a 94.9M reduced-decoder student and 154.9M best student.
sources.metric: Reconstruction quality/model compression, not our pose-acceptance criterion
sources.novelty_boundary: Generic small-model lunar distillation is prior art. Those student sizes also exceed our 100k-parameter constraint.

sources.title: Active Search for Real-Time Vision
sources.finding: Uses state uncertainty and predicted measurements to guide image search and information/cost decisions.
sources.novelty_boundary: Active patch acquisition is not new as a general idea.

sources.title: Back to the Feature: Learning Robust Camera Localization from Pixels to Pose
sources.finding: Learns multiscale features for geometric 6DoF localization against a 3D model and joint keypoint/pose refinement.
sources.metric: Camera localization under its own initialization/evaluation conditions
sources.novelty_boundary: Learning features for geometric camera refinement is established prior art.

interpretation: No universal or lunar state-of-the-art rank is inferred from these heterogeneous published scores. No new matcher, dataset, metric, or acceptance policy is run or selected here.
